description: Proposal texts for the `commitlore guard` suite, against spec/fixtures/guard/records.json. `reproposals` must be flagged; `unrelated` must not. The unrelated set is the false-positive measurement the ticket AC names: ten proposals a competent engineer could make in this same repository on the same afternoon, none of which revives anything that was ruled out. They are deliberately adjacent to the records — caches, sessions, expiry, queues — because ten proposals about unrelated subject matter would measure nothing.

reproposals.why: the plainest re-proposal: the rejected product, named

reproposals.text: use a redis instance to store sessions
reproposals.why: shares one word out of six with the alternative — Jaccard alone would miss it

unrelated.text: Add a retry with jitter around the outbound webhook call so a single 502 does not drop the event.
Rename the config key SESSION_TTL to SESSION_TTL_MS and update the two call sites.
Extract the expiry arithmetic in src/cache.ts into a small helper so the eviction test can call it directly.
Write a unit test that covers the branch where the entry has already expired.
Bump the Node engine field to 22 and drop the polyfill import.
Return a 404 instead of a 500 when the profile lookup finds nothing.
Add a structured log line with the request id so the p99 latency can be attributed to a route.
Move readSession and writeSession behind an interface so the tests can substitute a fake.
Debounce the settings form so we stop firing a save on every keystroke.
Document the eviction rule in the README and link it from the module header.

dogfood.description: Measured against CommitLore's own history, which is the only corpus large enough to show the failure that a seeded four-record repository hides: dozens of real rejections, so ordinary words like `rename`, `document`, `readme` and `regex` recur across many of them and stop being evidence. The first four `clean` entries are the CTO's verbatim reproduction cases, which scored 0.46–0.54 under the flat keyword rule and flagged; the rest are plausible work in this repository on any given afternoon. `flagged` are real re-proposals of rejections this repository actually recorded, keyed by `Record-Id:` rather than sha because identity survives rebase (SPEC §3.3) and a sha does not.
